findings.issue: The fixture makes successful teardown depend on a separately scheduled host-wide /bin/ps child exiting within 50 ms, independently of the enclosing 250 ms/one-second cleanup and five-second fixture budgets. Ordinary user-space scheduling or host inventory cost can therefore turn a correct lifecycle into an inventory TimedOut failure. The retained exact-head post-push suite actually failed 14/15 with that error in the stalled-join family, while the later focused family run passed. This is a concrete intermittent helper failure; unchanged helper bytes and rerunning to green do not cure it.
findings.recommendation: Redesign inventory acquisition so test success does not depend on an individually scheduled host-wide command meeting an ambient 50 ms speed condition. Prefer a deterministic kernel/session inventory interface scoped to owned processes, retaining one hard absolute cleanup lifetime and explicit ownership/reap of any subprocess. Keep the stopped-inventory failure proof separate from healthy lifecycle assertions. Do not mask the observed failure with retries, sleep padding, suppressed timeout errors or widened lifecycle budgets.
findings.evidence: process_ids:227-228 caps every inventory invocation at min(caller deadline,now+50ms), including preflight/diagnostic enumeration. Inventory::finish:190-197 kills/reaps then returns TimedOut; drain and cleanup retain that error even if subsequent cleanup succeeds. qa-7/startup-postpush-lifecycle.log records first stalled-worker case completed at5.139028833s, then owned session inventory timed out and lifecycle_supervisor_kills_and_reaps_stalled_join_families FAILED; final14passed/1failed. qa-7/startup-postpush-stalled-family-recheck.log later passes. Retained original failure copied unchanged to qa-8/flaky-retained-lifecycle-failure.log. Exact slow invocation, process state and scheduler delay were not logged, so their precise cause/phase is not asserted.
